sections.skill: Measure useful actions and conversion rate

questions.prompt: What is a useful action?

choices.text: A like on a stock photo
A visit that lasts one second
A booking, order, sign-up or call

questions.correct_answer: A booking, order, sign-up or call
questions.intro: Count what matters. VISITS show how many people came, but USEFUL ACTIONS show whether the site works: bookings, orders, sign-ups, calls. CONVERSION RATE = visits that included at least one useful action / total visits. Example: 20 of 800 visits included an order, so 20 / 800 = 2.5 percent. Track where visitors came from, and change one thing at a time so you know what made the difference. A big number of visits with no actions means the page is not doing its job.

questions.prompt: 12 of 400 visits included an action. What percent is that?
questions.intro: A rate compares a part to a whole. Conversion rate = visits with an action / total visits, then times 100 for a percent. Example: 15 of 500 visits included a booking: 15 / 500 = 0.03 = 3 percent. To predict actions, multiply visits by the rate: 1,000 visits at 3 percent = 0.03 x 1,000 = 30. Check that the percent is reasonable: visits with an action cannot exceed total visits, so this rate cannot pass 100 percent.
